bodyMarkdown:
OneSec is a well-regarded iOS app that adds a mandatory breathing pause before selected apps open. The idea is to interrupt the automatic, mindless open, give your brain a second to decide whether you actually want to open TikTok, or whether the urge is just habit.

The problem: OneSec is iOS-only. Android users looking for the same friction-before-apps experience need a different tool.

This guide covers the best OneSec alternatives for Android, from native Android features that do something similar, to dedicated app blockers that go further than a pause screen.

## What Makes OneSec Different

OneSec's core mechanic is the interruption: a breathing animation plays for a few seconds before your blocked app opens. This turns an automatic open into a conscious one. Most users report that this brief pause is enough to break the reflex about 40–60% of the time.

OneSec doesn't block the app, the app opens after the pause. It just adds friction at the moment of highest automaticity.

## Android Alternative 1: Android Pause Point (Native, Free)

Google added Pause Point to Android Digital Wellbeing in May 2026. It works almost identically to OneSec: selected apps trigger a brief pause before opening. No block, just friction.

**How to enable it:** Settings → Digital Wellbeing & parental controls → Pause Point → select apps.

This is the closest direct equivalent to OneSec on Android. It's free, built in, requires no download and works system-wide on any app.

**Limitation:** no session context, no tracking, no companion reactions, no block (just pause). If the pause isn't enough to break your habit, Pause Point won't add more.

## Android Alternative 2: CogniFocus (Best for Active Session Blocking)

CogniFocus takes a different approach from OneSec. Instead of a pause before every open, CogniFocus blocks selected apps during active focus sessions. You start a session, Shield activates and any blocked app that opens is caught before it loads.

The Goblin companion reacts when a block is caught, a visible mood change that creates accountability. Recovery nudges help you return to focus when you drift, rather than treating a distraction as a session failure.

**Why this is better than OneSec for heavy scroll habits:** Pause Point and OneSec rely on willpower to stop at the pause screen. If your habit is strong enough, you'll breathe for three seconds and open the app anyway. CogniFocus doesn't let the app open during an active session, the block is real, not just advisory.

**How to set up as an OneSec alternative:**
1. Download CogniFocus from Google Play.
2. Add your automatic-open apps (TikTok, Instagram, Reddit, YouTube) to the block list.
3. Grant Usage Access and Overlay permissions.
4. Start a session when you sit down to work or study.
5. Shield blocks any listed app that opens during the session.

CogniFocus Pro's Manual Block extends this to non-session windows, similar to OneSec's "block during evening" feature.

[Get CogniFocus on Google Play →](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.ionic.cognifocus)

## Android Alternative 3: AppBlock (Most Customisable Schedule-Based Blocker)

AppBlock is available on both Android and iOS and offers the most granular scheduling of any blocker. You can set different block rules for different times of day and different days of the week.

Unlike OneSec (pause) or CogniFocus (session-based block), AppBlock is schedule-based, you define windows rather than starting sessions. This works well if your distraction patterns are predictable and schedule-driven.

**Best for:** users with consistent schedules who want different rules at different times. Less suitable if your distraction patterns are session-based or unpredictable.

## Android Alternative 4: Stay Focused (Best Usage Analytics)

Stay Focused is a strong Android-specific blocker with good usage tracking. You can see exactly where your screen time is going, which is useful for understanding which apps are actually costing you focus time before deciding what to block.

The blocking is functional but passive, it shows a screen you can dismiss. For users who respond to data and awareness, Stay Focused's analytics are more detailed than any other option here.

**Best for:** building awareness of patterns before committing to harder blocks.

## Comparison: OneSec vs Android Alternatives

| Feature | OneSec (iOS) | Android Pause Point | CogniFocus | AppBlock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform | iOS only | Android native | Android | Android + iOS |
| Mechanism | Pause before open | Pause before open | Block during session | Schedule-based block |
| Blocks the app? | No | No | Yes (during session) | Yes (on schedule) |
| Cost | ~$2.99/month | Free | Free to start | Free tier + Pro |
| Companion reactions | No | No | Yes (Goblin) | No |
| Session streaks | No | No | Yes | No |

## Which Should You Choose?

If you want the OneSec experience on Android exactly: **Android Pause Point**, it's native, free and works the same way.

If the pause isn't enough and you need a real block: **CogniFocus**, blocks during sessions, Goblin reacts, recovery nudges help you return.

If you want schedule-based blocking across all times: **AppBlock**.

If you want to understand your patterns before blocking: **Stay Focused**.

The honest recommendation for most Android users: start with Pause Point for background friction, add CogniFocus for dedicated work sessions. Two friction layers are more effective than one.

[Download CogniFocus on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.ionic.cognifocus), free to start.
